name: Enrichment plant

real.plant: Urenco USA National Enrichment Facility, Eunice, New Mexico (Urenco)
real.basis: Urenco USA produces about 4.3 million SWU a year with more than 500 staff and long-term contractors (World Nuclear News, 2025), against the 4,100 SWU an hour of 100 kg of HALEU, its HEU line at the same scale; its power and water are not published

bpBasis: Urenco has invested about $5 billion in its National Enrichment Facility at Eunice (World Nuclear News, 2025)

name: Fuel fabrication plant

real.plant: Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility, Hopkins, South Carolina (Westinghouse)
real.basis: Columbia can fabricate 1,500 t of uranium a year (NRC record of decision, 2022), taken as fuel, and employs more than 1,000 people (Westinghouse); every fuel runs at that scale; its power and water are not published

bpBasis: The INL Fuel Cycle Cost Basis (Module D1-1, 2023) gives $629.1M overnight (2017 dollars) for a 520 tU a year oxide fuel plant, scaled linearly to the 1,500 t a year of the Columbia plant, $1.81B

name: Fission reactor
bpBasis: Sized by its 1 MW of electricity; the INL literature review of advanced reactor costs (INL/RPT-23-72972, 2023) gives a medium overnight capital cost of $13,000 a kWe for a microreactor (2019 dollars), so $13M without the fuel

name: Reprocessing plant

real.plant: Orano la Hague reprocessing plants UP2-800 and UP3-A, Beaumont-Hague, France (Orano)
real.basis: La Hague may treat 1,700 t of used fuel a year in its two plants (Orano, nuclear safety report 2023), against the recipe's 2,000 kg of uranium an hour; Orano la Hague has about 3,000 employees; the site used 595 GWh of energy in 2024 (Orano annual report 2024), 67.9 MW on average, all energy and not electricity alone; its water is not published

bpBasis: The INL Fuel Cycle Cost Basis (Module F1, 2021) gives $6.2B (2003) for La Hague UP3 at 800 tHM a year, scaled linearly to the 1,700 t a year of both plants, $13.2B

name: RTG factory

real.plant: Plutonium-238 supply programme, HFIR and REDC at Oak Ridge (US Department of Energy, for NASA)
real.basis: Oak Ridge is to make 1.5 kg of heat source plutonium oxide a year by 2026 (ORNL), taken as plutonium-238; the reactor and hot cells are shared with research, so its staff, power and water are not published

bpBasis: Reconstituting plutonium-238 production was estimated to cost upwards of about $235 million by 2017 (AIP FYI, from GAO)

real.plant: Heavy Water Plant Manuguru, Telangana, India (Heavy Water Board)
real.basis: Manuguru has a capacity of 185 t of heavy water a year, 37.2 t of deuterium at 20.1% deuterium in D2O, with about 1,485 employees, 81 MW of power and 180,000 m3 of river water a day, 7,500 t an hour (Heavy Water Board plant page, 2005)

name: Fusion plant
bpBasis: Sized by its 1 GW of electricity; the 2017 Bechtel cost study for ARPA-E judged that its 150 MWe fusion concepts might scale to $2 to $6 a watt at 1 GWe, and the midpoint, $4 a watt, gives $4B

name: Solar power station
bpBasis: Sized by its 100 MW; the NASA OTPS Space-Based Solar Power report (2024, fiscal 2022 dollars) costs the assembly of its cheaper 2 GW design, the heliostat swarm, at $78.9B, development left out, scaled linearly to $3.9B
